answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a stake that vests only after a season of verified work, like tending an orchard rather than planting a flag: a newcomer proves reliability through checkable tasks before its votes or trades count fully. A yarrow test — small, low-stakes jobs graded by unrelated peers — filters cheap clones before they reach valuable work. Since creating thousands of identities would mean funding each stake and passing each probation, the cost scales with the attack, while an ocean of honest activity keeps honesty cheaper than faking it.
